column_notes.min_grade: Empty means the course states no minimum grade — open entry, the most permissive value, not a missing one.
column_notes.tuition_kes: Empty means no fee could be sourced. It does NOT mean free; a genuinely free course carries 0.

fee_basis.published: The institution publishes this figure for this course.
fee_basis.derived: Worked out by applying a published rate to this course. The rate is sourced; the total was calculated.
fee_basis.illustrative: Sourced, but not the institution's own price for this course.
fee_basis.unpublished: No fee published. The cell is empty — this does not mean free.
fee_basis.unsourced: A figure carrying no citation. Legacy records only; no new record may ship this way.

courses.verification_note: Programme named in Baringo Technical College's published artisan course list. The college states that entry to the artisan level is open on a KCPE certificate alone, so no KCSE mean grade is recorded rather than a grade being inferred - a learner with any KCSE result, or none, meets the published bar. Artisan courses are stated to run one year. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026). Artisan fees vary more than diploma fees and published per-institution figures conflict, so treat this as an order of magnitude and confirm with the registrar.

Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026), not quoted by the institute for this course - confirm with the registrar.

Entry grade and structure from KUCCPS and TSC: the P1 certificate has been phased out and the Diploma in Primary Teacher Education is now the minimum qualification TSC will register, entered on a KCSE mean grade of C plain over three years at one of 33 public teacher training colleges, with placement through KUCCPS and assessment by KNEC. Fee derived from the Ksh 67,189 first-year figure published for KUCCPS-placed students at public TTCs - the same government consolidated rate used across public TVET - scaled to three years; one college separately quotes about Ksh 205,000 for the full course inclusive of admission, practicum and KNEC assessment, which agrees within two per cent. Outcome figures are null rather than estimated: with roughly 369,000 registered teachers unemployed, any employment rate Njia invented here would be actively misleading. Confirm fees with the college.

Published 2026 figures give a diploma range of roughly Ksh 115,950 to 226,700 and IATA programmes from Ksh 125,900 to 197,700, with accommodation about Ksh 18,000 a month and a Ksh 1,000 application fee. EASA does not publish a per-course fee in any source reachable from here, only those institution-wide ranges, so no figure is shown. A midpoint of a band that spans nearly two to one is not a fee: Ksh 171,000 appears in no source, and it was displayed identically on a 36-month diploma and an 18-month one - a number a reader would budget against, against a duration it does not describe. The sentence that carried it also claimed 'the middle of the published diploma range' while the certificates showed the bottom of the IATA range instead, so the note did not describe its own records. Ring the school for the fee for your specific programme, and budget separately for accommodation at about Ksh 18,000 a month and the Ksh 1,000 application fee.

The Kenya School of Law is a state corporation established under the Kenya School of Law Act, and this is the one programme it runs that a school leaver can enter directly - placement is through KUCCPS, which opened the May 2026 intake in February 2026. Published entry is a KCSE mean grade of C plain with at least a C+ in English or Kiswahili, so the subject grade is the real gate and a C plain alone is not enough. Alternative routes are published too: one principal pass at KACE, a pass in a certificate of law course at an accredited legal education provider, or a certificate of experiential learning from the Council of Legal Education. Two academic years minimum, three maximum. Teaching runs at the Karen campus and the Nairobi Town campus on Moi Avenue, weekday in-person days with virtual evening classes. Njia does not list the Advocates Training Programme, which is the school's better-known course: it is postgraduate and requires a law degree, so it is not a route from KCSE and listing it here would mislead. The school sets its own fees and does not publish a figure for this programme in any source reachable from this build, so it could not be verified and no figure is shown rather than a guessed one - ring the school for the current schedule.

Entry grade and structure from KUCCPS and TSC: the P1 certificate has been phased out and the Diploma in Primary Teacher Education is now the minimum qualification TSC will register, entered on a KCSE mean grade of C plain over three years at one of 33 public teacher training colleges, with placement through KUCCPS and assessment by KNEC. Confirm fees with the college.

Programme named in Nyandarua National Polytechnic's published course list. The polytechnic publishes its artisan (Level 4) entry as a KCPE or KCSE mean grade of D- and E, so an E clears the published bar and E is recorded - the same reading applied at Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti, where a KCPE certificate is an alternative to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it. As a national polytechnic it is legally empowered to train and award artisan, craft, diploma and higher diploma qualifications, and it runs more artisan programmes than the one listed here; only what a reachable source actually names is recorded. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026), which the Ministry of Education has directed all public TVET institutions to charge; government capitation of up to Ksh 30,000 a year reduces what a placed student actually pays, so treat this as the gross figure and confirm with the registrar.

Programme named in Siaya National Polytechnic's published artisan course list (formerly Siaya Institute of Technology). The institution's published artisan minimum is given as a KCPE certificate or a KCSE mean grade of D-. A KCPE certificate is an alternative to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it, so a learner holding an E clears the published bar and E is recorded. That is the same reading already applied at Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti, whose published minimum has the identical shape. Recording the D- branch instead removed this course from the screen of the learner least likely to have another option, and left Siaya reading as blind to an E-grade learner while its own national polytechnic sat in the catalogue. Ask the registrar whether KCPE alone is accepted. KNEC modular courses are being phased out for CBET, so confirm which curriculum the current intake runs. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026). Artisan fees vary more than diploma fees and published per-institution figures conflict, so treat this as an order of magnitude and confirm with the registrar.

Chuka University is a public chartered university and had not been listed here at all. Programme named in its published course listing; degrees are placed through KUCCPS at the national minimum of a KCSE mean grade of C+, with cluster-point cut-offs that move every cycle, so C+ is the floor to be eligible to apply rather than a guarantee of a place - check the current cut-off on the KUCCPS portal. It does not publish a single per-programme price: Kenya retired the Differentiated Unit Cost in May 2023 for the Student-Centred Funding Model, under which what a student pays is set by an assessed means band, so no fee is shown rather than a guessed one. The university also runs 25 diploma and 20 certificate programmes, which enter well below C+ and are the more useful route for many readers here; their individual names were not published in any source reachable from this build, so they are not listed and are worth asking about.

Programme named in its published course listing; degrees are placed through KUCCPS at the national minimum of a KCSE mean grade of C+, with cluster-point cut-offs that move every cycle, so C+ is the floor to be eligible to apply rather than a guarantee of a place - check the current cut-off on the KUCCPS portal. It does not publish a single per-programme price: Kenya retired the Differentiated Unit Cost in May 2023 for the Student-Centred Funding Model, under which what a student pays is set by an assessed means band, so no fee is shown rather than a guessed one. The university also runs 25 diploma and 20 certificate programmes, which enter well below C+ and are the more useful route for many readers here; their individual names were not published in any source reachable from this build, so they are not listed and are worth asking about.
